title: Sympathetic Nerve Activity and Aortic Aneurysm
content: Sympathetic hyperactivity contributes to the development and progression of numerous diseases, including cardiovascular disorders. This review examines the relationship between sympathetic hyperactivity and aortic aneurysms, including both abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) and thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA), conditions that often progress to aortic dissection, rupture, and death. The review first summarizes the distribution of adrenoceptors within the aorta and then discusses the role of sympathetic hyperactivity in the pathogenesis of AAA and TAA. Finally, it evaluates the perioperative use of beta-1 selective blockers and alpha-2 adrenoceptor agonists during open surgical repair of aortic aneurysms. Overall, the available evidence suggests that sympathetic hyperactivity is an important contributor to aortic aneurysm pathogenesis and progression to aortic dissection or rupture. In addition, perioperative administration of beta-1 selective blockers and alpha-2 adrenoceptor agonists, initiated at least 8 days before surgery, may confer cardiovascular benefits in patients with aortic aneurysm undergoing open surgical repair. Well-designed randomized clinical trials are needed to determine the effectiveness of sympatholytic therapies in preventing aortic aneurysm development and progression to aortic dissection or rupture.
